tasks.title: Challenger rebid only while open and without a backwards ask
tasks.spec:
Add Config.challenger_open_only: bool = False. This modifies only the existing challenger_rebid helper when both flags are enabled and the session has multiple suppliers; with the new flag off, preserve existing behavior exactly. Candidate selection must require challenger.status == 'open', never final_offer or agreed. Recheck that condition after any pending response and immediately before reserving a send. If a queued challenger becomes final_offer or agreed, complete the existing ticket and re-rank actual offers without sending a rebid, hold message or confirmation to that challenger. Add one economic guard before dispatch: find the challenger's latest actually sent, single-sheet priced buyer proposal from its event history. Validate and cost its complete package using that supplier's standards. The new rebid must have C at least as high as that previous buyer proposal, strictly below the incumbent's valid quoted C, and strictly below the challenger's current valid standing C. If the previous proposal is unavailable or cannot be compared reliably, or no proposal meets these bounds, finish the ticket without sending; do not relax the bounds or synthesize a new target. Keep existing clock boundaries, closing-slot reserves, ownership, one-ticket limit and post-response re-ranking. Do not extend the incumbent's clock, change acceptance economics, or use historical alternatives as executable primaries. Log status skips and the previous-proposal/request/incumbent costs. Tests must cover a final challenger at selection, an open challenger becoming final while queued, a backwards request, an eligible open challenger, and flag-off equivalence.

Keep every 'old' snippet short and unique; 3 coders work in parallel - touch only what your idea needs. No private keys on arena messages; never deepcopy threads; log exceptions.
tasks.hypothesis: Retain the useful part of G2-9—one chance for an unfinished challenger to respond to a fresh bar—without asking a finalized supplier to reopen or abruptly reversing the buyer's concession path.
tasks.risk: The guard may deliberately suppress every additional rebid in the sandbox. An eligible open challenger can still reject the request; this is risk reduction, not a guarantee of a better incumbent price.

tasks.title: Monotone late price asks on an unchanged package
tasks.spec:
Add Config.late_price_continuity: bool = False and append a final MESO_HOOKS entry after the existing package hooks. Implement a pure helper with signature (t, c_goal, picks). Activate only for a non-relationship multi-supplier RFQ, status open, one ordinary priced sheet, certain/live thread state, and sufficient existing message/clock reserve for a response and close. Derive history from t.events rather than round counters or a shared cache. Require at least two actually sent priced buyer proposals; the latest buyer proposal, proposed sheet, and latest two supplier primary sheets must have identical completed non-price terms. Require the supplier's latest primary price to have fallen. Skip conditional repairs, recalled confirmations, price-freeze trades, and any response since the last buyer proposal carrying a new attachment or an explicit revised-cost statement. Trigger only when the ordinary proposed unit price is below the last actually sent buyer price. Replace only unit_price with the previous buyer price plus one engine price tick, using the engine's existing two-decimal monetary precision and exact decimal arithmetic. Apply only if this price remains strictly below the supplier's current price and its actual C remains strictly below both the current standing package and the valid outside alternative. Revalidate allowed options, fixed terms, must-haves, full coverage and recorded supplier requirements; otherwise return picks unchanged. This is an explicit, bounded relaxation of the current goal: allow no more than the previous proposal's C plus the cost of that single tick. Do not change target_c, goal(), acceptance rules, message count or supplier statuses. Log the ordinary goal, previous dispatched proposal, replacement proposal and their costs. Tests must distinguish a moving-reference regression from a genuine new-evidence reanchor, preserve earned delivery terms, and prove no effect for single suppliers or final offers.

REVIEWER NOTES (team lead): Your Config flag ALREADY EXISTS - do NOT edit Config. All gen-1/gen-2 code is in the source. Implement ONLY the new method Negotiator._late_price_continuity_package(self, t, c_goal, picks) -> list of term dicts or None. It is ALREADY registered in MESO_HOOKS (runs after the other hooks); do NOT edit meso, _meso_core or MESO_HOOKS. Keep every 'old' snippet short and unique; 3 coders work in parallel - touch only what your idea needs. No private keys on arena messages; never deepcopy threads; log exceptions.
tasks.hypothesis: The transcripts show our price moving backwards even after useful supplier concessions. Maintaining a tiny visible forward move on the same delivered package may elicit a better pre-final response without extra rounds or post-final pressure.
tasks.risk: This intentionally spends a small amount of concession budget and may produce a slightly dearer agreement. It should not run after new cost evidence because a genuine reanchor can justify a firmer ask.

tasks.title: Conditional award language on the last open price-only ask
tasks.spec:
Add Config.open_close_intent: bool = False. Add a pure message helper called at the end of the ordinary Negotiator.write path; leave the safe_claims early-return path unchanged. Activate only for non-relationship multi-supplier RFQs, status open, a valid and certain live thread, exactly one ordinary sheet, and a recipient whose current primary is the lowest evaluated valid current offer across suppliers. The proposal must change only price relative to that primary after completing terms with the recipient's standards; its C must improve the standing offer and beat the valid outside alternative. Require either a non-negated supplier invitation to close/sign/finalize/wrap up in the latest message, or a proposed cost gap no larger than the supplier's last observed cost reduction between two primaries with identical non-price terms. Skip repairs, historical-offer confirmations, frozen-price trades, final_offer/agreed, and insufficient response-plus-close reserve. Use event history to allow this wording at most once per supplier; do not spend the opportunity merely by drafting. Replace only the generic closing question with: 'If you confirm the attached complete package unchanged and it remains our lowest-cost compliant offer, we are ready to proceed directly to award. Please confirm the price with the delivery, payment and other terms exactly as attached.' Preserve the existing fact, breakdown argument, rival quote, references, attachments, warm acknowledgement and numerical sheet unchanged. Do not invent volume, exclusivity, timing guarantees, rival prices or a second award commitment. No extra message, waiting window, acceptance override or post-final push. Log the trigger and actual proposal gap. Tests must cover negated closing language, a more competitive rival, non-price changes, repeated drafting versus an actually sent message, and single-supplier equivalence.

tasks.hypothesis: A10 responds to 'let us wrap this up' with another generic question. A concrete, conditional award request may exchange closing certainty for the remaining small concession while explicitly preserving the delivery package.
tasks.risk: The supplier may simply repeat its current price or finalize earlier. The conditional award wording is intentionally not an unconditional promise, so its persuasive effect may be limited.
